say: You give it a straight-line situation: a table, a graph or an equation. It finds the **slope** (the rate of change) and the start value, then uses them to predict.
The slope is how much the answer changes for each $1$ step in $x$. The start value is the answer when $x = 0$.

how.higher: Higher level asks you to say what a slope means in context, or to write the line from a table, as a part worth 5 marks on either paper (2015, 2017, 2019).
how.ordinary: Ordinary level uses it on Paper 1 in 2022, 2023 and 2025: write the equation from a table or graph, say what the rate means, or solve for the unknown (5 or 10 marks).

example.question:
A plumber charges a call-out fee plus an hourly rate. The cost, in euro, of a job lasting $x$ hours is $C = 40 + 30x$.
(i) What do $40$ and $30$ mean?
(ii) A job costs $190$ euro. How many hours did it last?

steps.title: Read the rate and start
steps.say: The number with $x$ is the slope. The number on its own is the start value.

lines.text: The slope is $\hl{1}{30}$: the cost goes up $30$ euro for each extra hour.
The start value is $\hl{2}{40}$: the cost at $x = 0$, the call-out fee.

steps.title: Put the cost in
steps.say: The job costs $\hl{4}{190}$ euro. Put that in for $C$.

steps.title: Solve for the hours
steps.say: Take away the start value $\hl{2}{40}$ first. Then divide by the slope $\hl{1}{30}$.

higher.tip: When you explain a slope, say how $y$ changes for each $1$ step in $x$, with the units.

say: You give it three points, the corners of a triangle. It finds the **area**.
The key idea: slide one corner to $(0, 0)$. Then the area is $\tfrac{1}{2}|x_1y_2 - x_2y_1|$, using the other two corners.

how.higher: Higher level uses it as a part inside a Paper 2 coordinate geometry question: 15 marks in 2023 (Q3), and 5 marks in 2025 (Q7).
how.ordinary: Ordinary level asks for it on Paper 2 almost every year (2015 to 2020, and 2025), as a part of its own worth 5 or 10 marks.

example.question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices $A(3, 2)$, $B(7, 5)$ and $C(5, 9)$.

steps.title: Move A to the origin
steps.say: Slide the whole triangle so that $A$ lands on $(0, 0)$. Take $3$ from every $x$ and $2$ from every $y$.

steps.title: Substitute into the formula
steps.say: Call the new points $(x_1, y_1) = \hl{1}{(4, 3)}$ and $(x_2, y_2) = \hl{2}{(2, 7)}$. Put them into the area formula.

steps.title: Work it out
steps.say: Do the multiplications first. The bars mean the answer is never negative.

higher.tip: Show the translation of one point to $(0, 0)$. It is credited by itself.

say: You give it a line with an unknown number in its equation, and a condition such as **parallel** or perpendicular to another line. It finds the unknown.
The key idea: the condition becomes an equation in the slopes. Parallel lines have equal slopes. Perpendicular lines have slopes that multiply to $-1$.

example.question: The line $kx + 4y = 7$ is parallel to the line $6x - 2y = 5$. Find the value of $k$.

steps.title: Slope of the first line
steps.say: Make $y$ the subject. The number in front of $x$ is the slope.

steps.title: Make the slopes equal
steps.say: Parallel lines have the same slope. Set $\hl{1}{-\tfrac{k}{4}} = \hl{2}{3}$ and solve for $k$.

lines.text: Check: with $k = -12$ the first slope is $-\tfrac{-12}{4} = 3$.

say: You give it two points, $A$ and $B$, and a ratio $m : n$. It finds the point $P$ on the segment $[AB]$ that splits it in that **ratio**.
The key idea: the segment is $m + n$ equal parts, and $P$ is $m$ parts from $A$. Each coordinate is a weighted average of the two ends.

how.higher: Higher level uses it as a 5 or 10 mark part inside a Paper 2 coordinate geometry question (2015, 2017, 2021, 2022, 2024). A translation method is accepted as well as the formula.

example.question: The points are $A(-3, 4)$ and $B(7, -1)$. The point $P$ lies on $[AB]$ so that $|AP| : |PB| = 2 : 3$. Find the coordinates of $P$.

steps.title: Match the numbers
steps.say: Here $m : n = 2 : 3$, $(x_1, y_1) = (-3, 4)$ and $(x_2, y_2) = (7, -1)$. The formula is $\left(\dfrac{nx_1 + mx_2}{m + n},\ \dfrac{ny_1 + my_2}{m + n}\right)$.

lines.text: $P$ is closer to $A$, because its part of the ratio is the smaller one.

steps.title: Find the x-coordinate
steps.say: Put the $x$ values and the ratio into the formula.

steps.title: Find the y-coordinate
steps.say: Do the same with the $y$ values.

higher.tip: You can skip the formula. Find the step from $A$ towards the first part, then multiply it up. This is credited.
